source.title: Long-term functional outcome after conservative management of a fingertip amputation with exposed bone, using a semi-occlusive dressing: a case report

presentation: On 23 April 2020, a 47-year-old man with no relevant medical history presented to a primary care center after cutting vegetables with a mandoline slicer. He was right-hand dominant and worked as a university professor. Examination showed partial amputation of the right little-finger pulp, approximately 10 × 15 mm, with an exposed distal phalanx and no nail-bed involvement (Fig. 1A).

events.detail: Right little-fingertip amputation with exposed distal phalanx, clinically consistent with an Allen type II injury.
events.source_span: The diagnosis was a right little-fingertip amputation with exposed distal phalanx, clinically consistent with an Allen type II injury.

events.detail: Bleeding was controlled using direct pressure and limb elevation.
events.source_span: Bleeding was controlled with direct pressure and limb elevation.

events.detail: The wound was cleansed with sterile saline and superficial non-viable tissue was removed without bone shortening.
events.source_span: The wound was cleansed with sterile saline; no bone shortening was performed and only superficial non-viable tissue was removed.

events.detail: A transparent semi-occlusive polyurethane dressing (Tegaderm) was applied to the wound.
events.source_span: A transparent semi-occlusive polyurethane dressing (Tegaderm) was applied (Fig. 1B).

events.detail: Initial pain was managed with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and paracetamol.
events.source_span: Initial pain was controlled with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and paracetamol.

events.detail: Presence of malodorous serous fluid beneath the dressing and early granulation, without signs of infection.
events.source_span: At 1 week, malodorous serous fluid was present beneath the dressing, with early granulation but no increasing pain, fever, spreading erythema, or purulent discharge (Fig. 1C).
Granulation tissue was abundant after 2 weeks (Fig. 1D);

events.detail: Clinical coverage of the previously exposed bone was achieved.
events.source_span: the exposed bone was clinically covered by weeks 3 to 4 (Fig. 1E and F);

events.detail: Near-complete pulp reconstruction of the fingertip.
events.source_span: near-complete pulp reconstruction was present by weeks 5 to 6 (Fig. 1G and H).

events.detail: Preserved function, high esthetic satisfaction, and mild residual sensory alteration.
events.source_span: At three months, the patient reported preserved function, high esthetic satisfaction, and mild residual sensory alteration.

events.detail: An in-person clinic assessment was scheduled approximately 6 years after the injury.
events.source_span: Approximately 6 years after injury, the patient was contacted by telephone and scheduled for an in-person clinic assessment.

events.detail: QuickDASH score of 2.3/100, with mild residual sensory reduction requiring keyboard typing adaptation.
events.source_span: The QuickDASH score was 2.3/100[9]. The only functional adaptation was avoiding use of the injured right little finger during keyboard typing because of mild residual sensory reduction.
